plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of others' bids or strategies. This is because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (not your own), so bidding your value ensures you win whenever it's profitable to do so, and never lose when winning would be profitable. Since my value is $9, I will bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks overpaying. With no history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $40.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're still the highest). Overbidding risks paying more than your value if you win; underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my true value of $32 to maximize expected profit.
